caseno:
Civil Appeal No. 84 & 85 of 1982 
From Civil Revision No. 984 & 985 of 1978
lawyer:
T.H. Khan, Sr. Advocate with Abdul Wahab Mia, Advocate instructed by Syed Sakhawat Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Appellants. 
Faqueer Abdul Mannan, Advocate instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No. 1.
Miah A. Gafur, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No. 4 & 7.
parties:
Md. Alkas Ali And Others ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mansur Ahmed Khan And Others ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Badrul Haider Chowdhury, J: This appeal, namely, C.A. No. 84 of 1982, arises out of the judgment and order passed by a learned Judge of the High Court Division sitting singly in C.R. No. 984 of 1978. A partition suit, being Title Suit No. 66 of 1959 was filed by the plaintiff respondent in the Court of the First Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for partition of the suit property measuring .75 acres of land described in the schedule to the plaint. The plaintiff claimed -/8/- share of the suit property. His case was that he and the deceased defendant No. 1 Md. Ismail Miah, predecessor-in-interest of the present respondent Nos. 9 to 19, jointly purchased the suit land by registered kabala dated 6-10-1947 in equal shares. His further case was that the said defendant No. 1 Mohammad Ismail Mia in collusion with the defendant No. 2 Mujibul Mowla (since deceased) has created some fraudulent deeds and is trying to grab the property. The trial court passed a decree in preliminary form declaring the plaintiff's -/8/- annas share in the said preliminary decree. The Pleader Commissioner was appointed to make the partition of the suit land in terms of the preliminary decree. The pleader Commissioner submitted a report showing the suit property measuring 1.01 acres contrary to the plaint case of .75 acres and the different defendants filed objection against that report. Thereafter the plaintiff filed an application for amendment of the plaint that the deed writer wrongly stated .75 decimals in the kabala and necessary amendment should be made in the schedule showing 1.01 acres of land in place of .75. This application was rejected by the learned Subordinate Judge. Thereafter the High Court Division was moved in Civil Revision No. 984 of 1978. The learned Single Judge noticed that if the area of land shows an excess in the Commissioner's report, the excess land shall also be divided between the parties inasmuch as it is a suit for partition. This decision has been challenged and leave was granted to consider whether the High Court Division acted illegally and without jurisdiction in making such observation thereby "reopening a question of fact already concluded by the High Court Division". 

 2. Mr. T.H. Khan was heard at length. He could not show how he will be prejudiced as defendants in the event of the excess land being divided according to the respective share. He had no answer. A feeble attempt was made that this was a question of fact which had been concluded by the High Court Division in F.A. No. 245 of 1962 and F.A. No. 4 of 1963. This contention does not hold good. Those appeals were filed against the preliminary decree. Those appeals were dismissed .In F.A. No. 245 of 1962 Majibul Mowla was the appellant. He was not given any saham by the trial court and his appeal was directed against this decision. In F.A. No. 4 of 1963 Md. Ismail Mia was the appellant and that appeal was also dismissed. These appeals, therefore, had nothing to do with the question of the area of land which is available for the partition amongst the parties. Deed mentions the plot numbers and the area was given with the boundary. If according to the pleader Commissioner, the land which is butted and bounded, an excess of land is available for partition then there is no conceivable reason for the parties to feel aggrieved. On the contrary they have all the reasons to be happy to see the area of land had increased. In the case of Safiuddin Kazi alias Safiruddin V. Moslem Ali Howlader and others, 12 D.L.R. 266 Rahman J observed: 

 3. In C.A. No. 85 of 1982 arising out of Civil Revision No. 985 of 1978 the rule was disposed of by the High Court Division with an observation that while passing the final decree the court is required to decide and dispose of all ancillary issues so that the disputes relating to the property in the partition suit is finally disposed of once for all without giving rise to any further scope for multiplicity of proceedings. Then the Court further gave the direction to proceed with the suit and to decide right, title and interest of the subsequent purchaser in the suit property on the basis of their entitlement as successor to the original co-sharer "to their actual saham made in the preliminary decree and to pass the final decree accordingly". Such observations do not affect adversely any party and Mr. T.H. Khan could not make any grievance which requires our consideration as to the justification of such observation. The learned Single Judge merely expressed that all issues should be settled to avoid any multiplicity of proceeding. No exception can be taken to such observations.
